failure: Pacemaker battery depletion requiring surgical replacement
constraint: Must maintain cardiac pacing for 5-10 years without surgical replacement
mechanism: Pacemaker-mediated tachycardia (PMT) can be triggered by atrial threshold testing, leading to symptomatic hypotension and syncope, indicating that PMT episodes contribute to device-related adverse events.
intervention: Implement a mode switch from DDD to DDIR in the pacemaker programming to prevent PMT initiation and reduce unnecessary pacing, thereby conserving battery life.
expected_effect: Reduced pacing frequency and elimination of PMT episodes will decrease battery depletion rate, extending device longevity to 5-10 years without surgical replacement.
falsification_test: Conduct a clinical trial comparing battery lifespan in pacemakers programmed to DDD vs. DDIR mode over 5 years, monitoring for PMT episodes and battery voltage decline.
mechanism_source_span: "Device interrogation revealed the presence of pacemaker-mediated tachycardia (PMT)... Management focused on reprogramming the DR ICD. The most critical adaptation was a mode switch from DDD to DDIR"

source_evidence.source_title: When the Pacemaker Goes Rogue: Pacemaker-Induced Tachycardia, Syncope, and Car Crash.
source_evidence.source_span: A 78-year-old male with a history of ischemic heart disease with prior myocardial infarction, severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction, and a device-related implantable cardioverter defibrillator (DR ICD) was admitted following a road traffic accident due to a sudden loss of control of the vehicle following a syncope. Initial investigations ruled out acute coronary syndrome and did not point to neurological causes. Device interrogation revealed the presence of pacemaker-mediated tachycardia
